question.leadin: Identify some of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
question.text: King Nebuchadnezzar ("NEB-uh-kud-NEZZ-ur") of Chaldea ("cal-DEE-uh") built these structures for his wife Amytis ("AM-uh-tis") of Media. They consisted of terraces and irrigation structures that serviced a variety of luscious trees.
question.clue: According to Strabo, an early version of Archimedes' Screw was built for use at this location.

swap.text: This Mesopotamian civilization contained the city of Ashur and had rulers like Tigaleth-Pileser and Sennacherib. Its capital, Nineveh (NIN-ih-veh), hosted the largest library in the world at the time, built by Ashurbanipal.
swap.clue: Accounts of invasions by this empire written by king Taharqa record that its armies had their bowstrings eaten by field mice.

question.leadin: Answer the following about old world writing systems.
question.text: This writing system developed in Sumer was typically written with the use of a wedge-shaped reed stylus on clay tablets. It was similar to pictographs.
question.clue: Henry Rawlinson studied the Behistun Inscription for insight into this system, which is seen on the oldest complaint tablet.

swap.leadin: This ruler's grandmother forced everyone in his empire to agree to his ascension to the throne in the Loyalty Treaty of Naqi'a-Zakutu.
swap.text: Name this emperor, who constructed a namesake library in Nineveh.
swap.clue: He had earlier conquered the Elamite capital Susa, and that defeat of the Kushite armies near Memphis allowed him to take the Egyptian capital.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about Mesopotamia's earliest civilization, Sumer.
question.text: This Akkadian conqueror of Sumer is said to have founded the world's first empire. This king's daughter Enheduanna is the first recorded poet in history.
question.answerHtml: Sargon of Akkad [accept Sargon the Great or Sargon I]
question.clue: This ruler famously defeated Lugal-Zage-Si of Umma, the last Sumerian King.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the reign of Tiglath-Pileser III.
swap.text: Tiglath-Pileser ruled the "neo-" version of this empire, whose other leaders included Sennacherib and Ashurbanipal.
swap.clue: This empire's final defeat came when Harran fell, an act precipitated by the civil war that broke out between Sin-shar-ishkun and Ashur-etel-ilani.

question.leadin: Shalmaneser [shall-mah-NEE-ser] III, a king of this empire, defeated Syrian forces at the Battle of Qarqar ["car-car"].
question.text: Name this ancient empire. Ashurbanipul [ah-shur-BAH-nih-pall] and Sinsharushkin [sin-shar-ISH-kun] ruled this empire, which was conquered by the Babylonians in 608 B་C་E.
question.clue: Gyges of Lydia fell to the Cimmerians after he lost this empire's support for aiding the revolt of Psamtik I, who expelled their forces from Egypt to found the 26th dynasty.

swap.leadin: This civilization's Ubaid period is said to have been developed from the Samarra culture.
swap.text: Identify this civilization whose last king was Lugal-Zage-Si and whose Jemdat Nasr period followed its Uruk period. It developed cuneiform.
swap.clue: This civilization was the first to farm year-round by employing irrigation canals, and its priesthood worshipped Anu and Inanna.

question.leadin: Name some of the users of ceramics in the ancient world.
question.text: This ancient civilization used clay for building, for tablets on which they invented writing in the form of cuneiform, and for pottery, for which they invented the wheel.
question.clue: The last king of the Lagash dynasty, Lugal-Zage-Si was the last king of the ethnicity, conquering Uruk, where he established his capital.

swap.leadin: A piece found in this city has two sides: A side depicting a war scene and a side depicting a banqueting scene.
swap.text: Name this home of an artifact discovered by Leonard Wooley that got its name from the belief that it would be held up during parades. A massive structure in this city was restored by Nabonidus and dedicated to this city's patron deity, Nanna.
swap.clue: A king named -Nammu, who founded a dynasty that supplanted Lagash and the Gutians, was succeeded by Shulgi.

question.leadin: According to Herodotus, the prayers of the Pharaoh Sethos were answered when field mice destroyed the shields and bows of this man's army.
question.text: Name this son of Sargon II and father of Esarhaddon who returned to Nineveh after a plague inhibited his attempt to take Jerusalem from the Judean King Hezekiah.
question.clue: Though he compelled tribute, this ruler was prevented by a plague from capturing Jerusalem from Hezekiah.

swap.text: The British ambassador to Tewodros was Hormuzd Rassam, an Assyrian archaeologist who discovered the clay tablets containing this work about a king of Uruk, the oldest known piece of literature.
swap.clue: The Sumerian king list states this figure ruled between king Dumuzid and his own son Ur-Nungal. In an ancient story, this figure loses his friend Enkidu and learns the secret of immortality.

question.text: This Sumerian city, which the ancients considered the world's oldest, contained Enki's cult center, the E-Abzu or "House of Deep Waters." Silt accumulated in the Persian Gulf south of this city, where Amar-Sin built a ziggurat.
question.answerHtml: Eridu [or Irîtu; accept Tell Abu Shahrain; accept Eridu Genesis] (Eridu was once located on the sea, but the silt eventually shifted it over 100 miles inland.)
question.clue: This Mesopotamian city whose rulers are the first kings mentioned on the Sumerian King List, which is often taken as evidence for this city being the oldest in Sumerian civilization.

swap.text: The best example of a Sumerian schoolhouse was found in this city, which was the center of worship for Enlil. This city's Ekur Temple was rebuilt by Naram-Sin.
swap.clue: Fragments of Hammurabi's Code have been found in this city, whose "scribal corner" is rich with ancient texts. Various Mesopotamian dynasties sought to control this city of religious importance, the home of the god Enlil.

question.leadin: Objects such as an axe with a copper and gold handle adorned with a boar attest to the influence of these people's culture in Ugarit.
question.text: Name these people whose namesake language was primarily spoken in the Mitanni kingdom.
question.clue: This ethnic group largely made up the population of the Mitanni Kingdom to the southeast of the Hittite Empire. Kikkuli ("kee-KOO-lee") wrote a horse training manual in this ethnic group's namesake language, which was most closely related to Urartian.

swap.text: An Assyrian king with this name tried to build a capital at Dur-Sharrukin but died in a skirmish before it was done. Another ruler with this name was, like Moses, left in a basket in a river according to a forged "birth legend."
swap.answerHtml: Sargon [accept Sargon of Akkad or Sargon the Great or Sargon I; accept Sargon II]
swap.clue: The earliest known author, the priestess Enheduanna, was the daughter of a ruler of this name who legendarily served as a cupbearer to Ur-Zababa.

question.text: One of the languages in Darius the Great's Behistun Inscription was the language of these people, based at Susa. Their Old Kingdom was conquered by Shulgi of Ur, although they rebounded under Kutir-Nahhunte I.
question.clue: Another ruler of this kingdom installed his son Warad-Sin on the throne of Larsa.

swap.leadin: Matthew, a chronicler from this city, wrote the Zhamanakagrutyun.
swap.text: Identify this city once called Justinopolis which was conquered by Imad al-Din Zangi in 1144.
swap.clue: Jacob Baradaeus, a bishop of this city, was crucial in founding the Syriac Orthodox Church.

question.text: Non-cuneiform languages like Greek were used for Babylonian historical texts much earlier, such as by this 3rd-century BC priest who wrote the lost Babyloniaca.

swap.leadin: Daniel Fleming discussed "early collective governance" in this polity, which was mostly comprised of Sim'alite and Yaminite tribal confederations.
swap.text: Name this polity founded in the early Bronze Age, a major rival of Ebla. "Terrestrial" and "celestial" domains are delineated in a painting from this polity showing a ruler's "investiture."
swap.answerHtml: Mari [accept Tell Hariri] (The painting is the investiture of Zimri-Lim.)
swap.clue: While providing terminology for parts of the body, animals, and economic functions, the names of specific people are largely absent from a peace treaty between this city and Ebla.
